newsitem.title: USA: Duke sees 4-6 pct earnings dilution in '98.
newsitem.headline: Duke sees 4-6 pct earnings dilution in '98.

text.p: Duke Power Co executives said on Monday the merger with PanEnergy Corp was due to be completed in late 1997, and was expected to dilute Duke Power's earnings in 1998.
Duke, a utility company based here, said earlier Monday that it would absorb Houston-based PanEnergy in a stock deal to create Duke Energy Corp.

"We'll expect during the first full year of operations the combined entity might experience some earnings dilution in the range of four to six percent," Duke Power Chief Financial Officer Rich Osborne said.
Osborne made the comments to reporters on a conference call after the merger announcement. He was joined by Duke Power Chairman Bill Grigg and PanEnergy President Chief Executive Paul Anderson.
Osborne said by 1999, the second full year of the combined electricity and natural gas companies, the deal would become accretive to earnings.
"That transaction will turn accretive to our shareholders during the course of the second full year of operations and thereafter will be accretive," he said.
Chairman Grigg said by the year 2000 the merger would add an estimated $250 million a year to the new company's earnings. Afterwards, he said, earnings growth would range near double digits.
"Earnings growth going forward should be in the eight to 10 percent range," Grigg said.

Grigg, who became chairman in 1994, said he would retire next year when he turns 65. A spokesman said Duke Power does not have a mandatory retirement age but CEOs have routinely stepped down at age 65.
Grigg will be replaced by Richard Priory, currently president and chief operating officer at Duke Power.
The executives acknowledged some job responsibilities overlapped in the administrative area but they would not comment on potential layoffs.
Most of PanEnergy's markets are in the Northeast and Midwest, which will raise the national profile of Duke Power.

"As we envisioned expanding the electric business nationally we needed a platform on which to do that," Priory said. "Clearly, PanEnergy has a very extensive platform in 30 states and have gas positions in 48 states in North America."
"So that clearly leaves us with a platform to geographically expand our business and create a national presence in the delivery of energy," Priory said.
Grigg said customers in the Carolinas were not expected to see any immediate impact from the merger.
The two companies began discussing the merger last July.
Shares of Duke Power were down 1-3/4 at 46-1/8 while shares of PanEnergy rose 1-5/8 to 43-7/8 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
